title: AI receptionist: what it is and how to choose | Stacktik
metaDescription: An AI receptionist answers calls, takes messages and books appointments. Stacktik helps you choose one and connects it to your phone system and CRM.
h1: We help you choose an AI receptionist and connect it to your CRM.
lede: An AI receptionist is software that answers your business phone with a voice agent. It greets the caller, answers common questions, takes a message, books an appointment, routes the call and hands over to a person.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: A voice agent that answers business calls, takes messages, books appointments, routes callers and hands over to a person under rules you set.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales and customer-facing teams whose calls arrive faster than people can answer them, or after hours, and who want each call on the CRM record.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: A shortlist with monthly costs, the purchase handled if you want it, the agent connected to your phones and CRM, written rules and test calls.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: Software is on the vendor's own plan and pricing. Our implementation is a fixed fee, quoted in writing before work starts.

blocks.h2: AI receptionist vs virtual receptionist vs auto attendant.
blocks.intro: The three terms get used as if they meant the same thing. They do not.

items.title: Auto attendant: a phone menu
items.body: The caller presses a key or says a department name and the call is routed. It follows fixed rules.

items.title: Virtual receptionist: a human service
items.body: People at an outside company answer in your business name, take messages, book appointments and transfer calls.

items.title: AI receptionist: a voice agent
items.body: Software that holds a spoken conversation: it answers common questions, takes messages, books into your calendar, routes calls and hands over to a person.

items.title: AI answering service and AI voice agent
items.body: More names for the same category. The first usually means message taking and after-hours cover. The second, also called AI phone agent, covers outbound calls too.

items.title: A blend of AI and people
items.body: Some services put an AI agent on the first answer and human receptionists behind it for the calls it hands over.

items.title: How to tell which you need
items.body: A phone menu fits callers who only need a department, people fit calls that need judgement, and an AI receptionist fits the same few requests.

blocks.eyebrow: What it can and cannot do
blocks.h2: What an AI phone receptionist can and cannot do.
blocks.intro: An AI receptionist is good at the routine parts of a call and poor at the parts that need judgement.

items.title: Answer and route calls
items.body: It picks up on the lines and during the hours you choose, asks what the caller needs and sends the call to the right person or queue.

items.title: Take messages
items.body: It records who called, their number and what they asked. Connected to the CRM, the message lands on the caller's record with a callback task.

items.title: Book appointments
items.body: Working as an AI appointment setter, it offers open times from a calendar you connect and books the slot.

items.title: Answer common questions
items.body: Hours, location, services, what to bring. It answers from the information you provide.

items.title: What it cannot do
items.body: It does not exercise judgement. Complaints, exceptions, pricing commitments, upset callers and unusual requests belong with a person. It can also mishear names and numbers.

items.title: Hand over to a person
items.body: The handover is the part to design first: the caller asks for a person, the topic is on your list, or the agent is unsure.

blocks.h2: Choosing an AI receptionist for small business teams.
blocks.intro: A demo shows the easy call. These points separate one option from another once real callers are on the line.

items.title: Your phone system
items.body: Check how it takes calls from the system you already use: forwarded from your main number, on its own number, or inside your existing call flow.

items.title: Your CRM and calendar
items.body: Ask what it writes to the CRM after each call, and whether it does so directly or through a connector.

items.title: The handover
items.body: Ask how a transfer to a person works, what happens when nobody picks up and what happens outside business hours.

items.title: Languages and recordings
items.body: Check the languages it handles, where recordings and transcripts are stored, and what callers are told about recording and about speaking with an AI.

items.title: Pricing structure
items.body: Ask what the subscription, the usage charge by the minute or call, phone numbers and any setup fee add up to in a busy month.

items.title: Control after launch
items.body: Check who can change the greeting, the answers and the rules without going back to the vendor, and whether you can read transcripts.

blocks.h2: How Stacktik sets up an AI phone answering service.
blocks.intro: One technical RevOps consultant is assigned to your project and stays with it. The steps below are the usual order.

items.title: A free call
items.body: We go through how calls reach you today, what callers ask for, and what you use for phones and CRM.

items.title: A written proposal
items.body: Two or three options that fit your calls, each with its monthly cost and our relationship with the vendor stated next to its price.

items.title: The purchase, if you want it
items.body: Where it helps, we set the plan and phone numbers up through the vendor's partner program, in your name. You can also buy direct.

items.title: Connected to your phones and CRM
items.body: We connect the agent to your phone system and CRM. Each call creates or updates a record, with an owner and the next step set.

items.title: Rules and handover, in writing
items.body: We set what the agent answers, what it never answers, when it transfers and to whom, and what happens when nobody picks up.

items.title: Tested, trained, handed over
items.body: We test the common and awkward requests before the agent takes real calls, then train your team and hand over notes on how each piece runs.

platforms.h2: The platforms an AI receptionist sits between.
platforms.intro: An AI receptionist works between a phone system and a CRM. These are the platforms we set up or can source.

faq.a: An AI receptionist is software that answers business phone calls with a voice agent, in place of a keypad menu or a person. It greets the caller, answers common questions from information you provide, takes messages, books appointments, routes calls and hands over to a person under rules you set.

faq.q: How much does an AI receptionist cost?
faq.a: It depends on the vendor's plan and on how many calls you take, so there are no figures on this page. Plans are commonly built from a monthly subscription plus usage by the minute or by the call, with phone numbers and sometimes a setup fee.

faq.q: Is an AI virtual receptionist a person or software?
faq.a: Software, in most cases. The term is used two ways: as another name for an AI receptionist, and for a blended service where an AI agent answers first and people at an answering service take the calls it hands over.

faq.q: How do I choose an AI answering service?
faq.a: Start from your calls, not from a demo. List what callers ask for, which requests need a person and what has to be written to the CRM. Stacktik puts two or three options on a written proposal with the monthly cost of each.

faq.q: How do you set up an AI receptionist?
faq.a: In this order: a free call, a written proposal with a shortlist and costs, the purchase if you want us to handle it, the connection to your phone system and CRM, written rules for answers and handover, then test calls and team training before it takes real calls.

faq.q: What should I check when buying an AI receptionist in Canada?
faq.a: Check whether it answers in English and French, where call recordings and transcripts are stored, and what callers are told about recording and about speaking with an AI. Stacktik is based in Ontario and works with teams across Canada and the United States.
